document.title: Record reviewer decisions without losing product truth
document.summary: Reviewers can choose, explain, and record a product decision through the normal review-feedback channel while canonical approval remains explicit.
document.reviewFocus: Choose the retention policy, provide rationale, and verify that selected or confirmed browser input becomes agent-readable feedback without becoming approval.

sections.title: Reviewers can create an agent-readable decision record

items: A PRD contains a real unresolved choice
Select, explain, and record the choice through durable review feedback
Browser state does not approve canonical product truth

sections.title: Selections must not stop at ephemeral browser state

blocks.text: A reviewer could select an option and add rationale, but separate local export made that input invisible to the agent reading normal review comments.

blocks.title: Trust gap
blocks.text: An agent could mistake local completeness for product approval.

sections.title: Recording and approval remain separate actions

items.title: Select
items.text: The reviewer selects a known option or writes a custom answer.

items.title: Explain
items.text: The reviewer provides rationale and identifies the owner.

items.title: Record
items.text: Selection changes save anchored review feedback; the checkbox confirms that same record with rationale, owner, completeness, and source fingerprint.

items.title: Reconcile
items.text: The agent reads the normal review sidecar and updates canonical source only after explicit approval.

sections.title: A decision moves from question to canonical truth

blocks.question: How does a reviewer choice become portable without becoming implicit approval?
blocks.caption: The review record enters the same durable feedback channel as comments before explicit approval changes canonical truth.
walkthrough: Start from the unresolved reviewer question.
Record the selected option with rationale and owner.
Persist the selected or confirmed decision in the normal review sidecar, or export it when viewed standalone.
Apply only explicitly approved choices to canonical source.

sections.title: Record one review decision end to end

blocks.title: Record a reviewer choice through the review channel
blocks.outcome: A reviewer leaves one anchored, agent-readable decision record alongside comments.
blocks.boundary: The action does not mark the PRD Approved or modify its source.

story.capability: record a selected option with rationale
story.outcome: the product owner can reconcile an explicit decision

scenarios.title: Main scenario
scenarios.given: a report contains an unresolved product decision
scenarios.when: the reviewer selects an option, enters rationale and owner, and checks Decision recorded
scenarios.then: Pi HTML review writes a confirmed structured record to its comment sidecar, while standalone viewing retains local persistence and explicit Markdown export

scenarios.title: Incomplete record
scenarios.given: one required decision field is empty
scenarios.when: the reviewer tries to record the choice
scenarios.then: the checkbox remains unavailable and explains what is missing

steps.title: Choose
steps.context: The open decision shows real options and a custom answer.
steps.outcome: The rationale and owner fields become the next required work.

steps.title: Record
steps.context: Selection, rationale, and owner are complete.
steps.response: Pi HTML review upgrades the anchored selection feedback to confirmed review input.
steps.outcome: Finishing review writes the decision with comments to one agent-readable sidecar.

acceptance.text: Recording is unavailable until selection, rationale, and owner are present.
Standalone reload restores local input; Pi HTML review retains selected or confirmed input in the active review comment channel.
Sidecar or standalone export identifies the stable decision ID and source fingerprint and states that the record is not approval.

blocks.after: After this slice, the agent can read selected or confirmed decisions with normal comments without silently approving or modifying product truth.

sections.title: Stress the requirements together
sections.summary: Each requirement is traced through a BDD path, dependencies, interactions, collision check, and observable proof.

blocks.title: The approved product behavior composes as one coherent path
blocks.source: The requirement set defined by this PRD and its reviewed product evidence
blocks.path: actor trigger → product state change → decision → observable result
dependencies: The BDD scenario and acceptance criterion in the primary slice
interactions: The requirement constrains the shared behavior, scope, and acceptance boundary
blocks.resolution: The requirements are compatible because they describe one bounded actor outcome without contradictory permissions, states, timing, or recovery rules.
blocks.proof: The referenced BDD path and ac-001 provide an independently observable product result.

sections.title: Canonical approval stays outside browser persistence

items: In scope: one Pi HTML review sidecar for comments and selected or confirmed decisions.
In scope: standalone local persistence and Markdown export.
In scope: explicit distinction between review input and accepted truth.
Out of scope: automatic source-file mutation or implied approval.

sections.title: Choose how long local review input remains available

blocks.question: How long should browser-local review input remain available?

options.label: Persist until manually replaced or cleared

blocks.rationale: Review may span reloads before the exported record is reconciled.
